summary: A loading bar that can be driven by real async progress or simulated, with smoothing.
overview: Plug-and-play loading bar, and its documentation is blunt about the thing most loading bars get wrong: there is no single progress number Unity computes for you. There are only two real sources — an AsyncOperation's progress, and your own count of completed steps — and this can be driven by either, or told to simulate.
useCases: A scene-load bar driven by real progress.
A multi-step initialisation where you count the steps.
A deliberately simulated bar where there is nothing real to measure.

params.tuning: The visible bar chases the real target, so it never jumps. This is why a bar that leaps from 0 to 90 still looks like it filled.

gotchas.title: A simulated bar is a lie, and sometimes the right one
gotchas.body: It is offered explicitly rather than pretended to be real progress. Use it when there is genuinely nothing to measure, not to hide that you did not wire the real thing.
